title: intent <family> help is unrecognized on 9 of 11 families where v2 answered it, so the top-level help restore was a half-fix and command grammar is in scope for parity
body:
`intent <family> help` is unrecognized on 9 of 11 families, where v2 answered it. The top-level spelling was restored and the per-family one was not, which is the half-fix `0154` names.

DRIVEN, tree binary `abe69906`, verbs invoked in a project it initialised, exit codes taken without a pipe:

    intent help          rc=0   answers (tree)
    intent help          rc=2   refuses  (3.0.0 keg -- this is 0086, already dispositioned)

    intent st help       rc=1   error: unrecognized subcommand 'help'
    intent wp help       rc=1   error: unrecognized subcommand 'help'
    intent ac help       rc=1   error: unrecognized subcommand 'help'
    intent at help       rc=1   error: unrecognized subcommand 'help'
    intent todo help     rc=1   error: unrecognized subcommand 'help'
    intent issues help   rc=1   error: unrecognized subcommand 'help'
    intent claude help   rc=1   error: unrecognized subcommand 'help'
    intent agents help   rc=1   error: unrecognized subcommand 'help'
    intent lang help     rc=1   error: unrecognized subcommand 'help'

`doctor` and `sync` differ only because they take a positional argument and reject `help` as a bad value, so they are not evidence of the subcommand existing.

WHY THIS IS A PARITY GAP AND NOT A RATIFIED DEVIATION. `parity.md:7` puts **command/subcommand/flag grammar** in scope for parity, alongside stdout shape, the `ok:`/`error:` voice and exit codes. A subcommand v2 answered and v3 does not is a grammar difference, which is the one axis the contract holds rather than a deviation class it ratifies. The ratified classes are file layout, issues directories, generated-view banners, manual-edit workflows and `corrected`; a missing subcommand is none of them.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, because the route matters more than the row. Six core-family `.bats` files classified `keep` in the register fail under v3. vc ruled (2026-08-31, under hv's pen) that v2 message STRINGS are outside the narrowed contract, so those files want `deviate` with their assertions RETARGETED at v3 wording rather than deleted. Triaging `wp_commands.bats` before retargeting anything, so that a blind sweep could not paper over a real difference, separated the failures into classes -- and two were not wording:

  - `intent wp help` expecting `Usage: intent wp`, which is THIS row: a grammar difference, in scope.
  - three tests expecting `Work package not found` and getting `this project has not been migrated to Intent v3 -- it declares Intent 3.0.0, and 1 steel thread carries v2 canon this binary cannot read (ST0001)`, which is a FIXTURE that cannot construct under v3 and is cc's documented class (8 of 31 `keep` files, measured 2026-08-14).

So the retarget condition earned its keep before a single assertion was rewritten: had the six files been swept to v3 wording mechanically, this row would have been converted into silence rather than found.

RELATION TO EXISTING ROWS, checked rather than assumed. `0086` is the TOP-LEVEL `intent help` on the published keg plus its false remedy, and it is dispositioned; this row is the per-family spelling and is live at HEAD. `0162` is `intentd --help` starting a daemon, a different binary and a different mechanism. `0154` owns the class this is an instance of -- a fix landing on one spelling of a surface and not on its siblings.

NOT RULED HERE: whether the remedy is to add `help` to every family, or to declare the family-level spelling retired and correct the v2 tests to `--help`. The first restores parity as `parity.md:7` states it; the second is a deviation and would need ratifying as one rather than assumed. Either way the six `keep` rows cannot be retargeted until this is decided, because the assertion has no correct v3 target while the answer is open.

=== REMEDY PROPOSED 2026-09-02 18:22Z (dc), FOR vc TO RATIFY ===

**PROPOSAL: RESTORE `help` ON EVERY FAMILY, UNIFORMLY, AT rc=0.** Not the second option, and the measurement is why.

**THIS ROW'S OWN PREMISE DOES NOT SURVIVE A DRIVE.** It reads *9 of 11 families where v2 answered it*. Driven against the v2 trunk at HEAD, in a v2-stamped scratch project with `intent/st` present, each rc taken without a pipe:

    st      rc=1  ANSWERS  Usage: intent st <command> [options] [arguments]
    wp      rc=1  ANSWERS  Usage: intent wp <command> [options] [arguments]
    ac      rc=1  REFUSES  error: unknown ac command: help (try: list, status, ...)
    at      rc=1  REFUSES  error: unknown at command: help (try: list, lint, ...)
    todo    rc=1  ANSWERS  Usage: intent todo [command] [arguments]
    issues  rc=0  ANSWERS  Usage: intent issues <command> [options]
    claude  rc=1  REFUSES  error: Unknown claude subcommand. Try: intent claude ...
    agents  rc=0  ANSWERS  Usage: intent agents <command> [options]
    lang    rc=0  ANSWERS  Usage: intent lang <command> [options]

**v2 ANSWERS SIX OF THE NINE, REFUSES THREE, AND ANSWERS CLEANLY ON ONLY THREE.** `ac`, `at` and `claude` are refusals in v2 as much as in v3 -- so for those three there is no v2 behaviour to restore and no regression to name. Of the six that answer, three do it at rc=1.

**THIS ROW IS ITSELF INSTANCE-SHAPED.** It was found through `wp help` in `wp_commands.bats` -- a family where v2 does answer -- and generalised to nine. The generalisation was not driven. Recorded here rather than absorbed, because it is the class the estate has been finding all week.

**AND THE MEASUREMENT STRENGTHENS THE FIRST OPTION RATHER THAN THE SECOND.** Retiring the family-level spelling would have been the honest read if v2 had uniformly refused. It does not: it answers on six, refuses on three, and does it at two different exit codes. **Porting that is not parity -- it is the only outcome that cannot be stated in one sentence.** A uniform `help` at rc=0 is a superset of v2 on every family where v2 answered, and a strict improvement on the three where it refused. No v2 behaviour is lost in either direction.

**rc=0 AND NOT rc=1, ON A RULING THIS BUILD HAS ALREADY MADE.** `spine.rs` records INV-07: v2's `--help` reporting FAILURE on 10 of 27 commands is a DEFECT, not a contract, and v3 takes clap's exit-0 behaviour deliberately. The same reasoning covers `help`: matching v2's rc=1 on `st`, `wp` and `todo` would port at the family level the exact defect v3 declined to port at the root.

**WHERE IT IS, AND WHY THE ROOT ALREADY WORKS.** `spine.rs:307` sets `.disable_help_subcommand(true)`, which clap propagates down the tree, and the root is served by an EXPLICIT arm at `render.rs:75` (`Some(("help", _)) => help_root()`). **That is precisely the half-fix `0154` names: the root got a hand-written arm while the setting kept the spelling off everywhere else.**

**NOT DRIVEN, AND STATED AS SUCH: I HAVE NOT BUILT THIS.** A rebuild window is hv's (`0196`), so the change is proposed and not verified. Two things a build must check rather than assume: whether clearing the setting makes clap generate a `help` subcommand at the ROOT that collides with the explicit arm at `render.rs:75`, and whether the generated per-family help reads from the dispatch table the way the rest of the surface does. **Calling it a one-line change is the claim I am specifically not making.**

**WHAT IT UNBLOCKS.** The six core-family `keep` rows can be retargeted once this is ruled: their grammar question closes, and what remains is the WORDING retarget vc already ruled. `WP-05` follows.
